name: China
tagline: The joint-venture universities are the real English-taught route
summary: There are two Chinas in this file. The first is the elite domestic universities — Tsinghua, Peking, Fudan, Shanghai Jiao Tong — which admit international undergraduates through a separate application but teach the overwhelming majority of their bachelor's degrees in Mandarin. A handful of English-taught bachelor's programmes exist there, mostly in economics and international relations, and most international undergraduates spend a preparatory year on Chinese first. The second China is the joint-venture universities: NYU Shanghai, Duke Kunshan, Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool, Nottingham Ningbo, CUHK-Shenzhen, Wenzhou-Kean. These teach entirely in English, award a Western degree alongside a Chinese one, run Western admissions calendars, and are where a Danish IB student can realistically go without Mandarin. Duke Kunshan's deadlines for a 2027 start — Early Decision 2 November 2026, Regular Decision 4 January 2027 — are exactly the ones to build a plan around.
whyConsider: The joint-venture universities give you a fully English-taught degree and, usually, two diplomas: a Chinese one and an American or British one. Duke Kunshan awards both a US and a Chinese degree.
Deadlines work for IB students: Duke Kunshan's Regular Decision deadline is 4 January 2027, with an acceptance deadline of 1 May 2027 — a normal American calendar you can plan around.
Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool offers over 60 English-taught undergraduate programmes with a dual XJTLU and University of Liverpool degree, plus 2+2 and 2+1+1 routes that let you finish in Liverpool.

Chinese Government Scholarships (the CSC scheme) fund bachelor's degrees including tuition, accommodation, a living stipend and medical insurance, applied for through the Chinese embassy or directly through a university.
Tuition and living costs at the domestic universities are low by any international standard, and Mandarin is a genuinely valuable thing to spend four years acquiring.
watchOuts: We could not verify a single Chinese tuition figure, scholarship amount or domestic-university deadline from an official page in this research — most of the relevant sites blocked automated fetching. Nearly every numeric field is left blank here. Verify everything directly.

Peking University's Yenching Academy is a one-year master's programme, not an undergraduate route. Yuanpei College is PKU's liberal-arts honours college but teaches principally in Chinese. Neither is an English-taught bachelor's entry point.

At the domestic universities, 'international undergraduate admission' usually assumes HSK Chinese proficiency — typically HSK 4 to 6 depending on the programme — or a year of preparatory Chinese language study first. Do not assume English-taught.
Joint-venture tuition is high by Chinese standards: NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan charge near-American fees, though both offer substantial scholarships and need-based aid.

Political and academic conditions differ sharply from Europe. Internet access is restricted, academic freedom on certain topics is limited, and your ability to research some subjects will be constrained. Think about whether your intended field is affected.
Visa, residence permit and annual health-check requirements are administratively heavy, and rules change with relatively little notice.
Denmark's SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk before budgeting.

ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion. The joint-venture universities apply their Western parent's IB requirements; the domestic universities read the transcript within their own international admissions process.
notes: At the joint-venture universities the IB is standard currency and is read exactly as it would be by the parent institution in the US or UK.

At the domestic universities, the IB satisfies the secondary-education requirement, but admission usually also turns on Chinese language proficiency and, for some programmes, an entrance examination or interview.
Duke Kunshan operates a test-optional policy for standardised tests; it did not publish an IB score requirement on the page we read.
Minimum IB scores could not be verified for any Chinese institution in this research.

portal.name: No central portal, and no replacement for the one that has gone. Campus China (China Scholarship Council) was the official information and scholarship site and its domain no longer resolves; joint-venture universities use the Common Application or their own portals, and the Chinese universities publish inside login-gated application systems of their own.

deadlines.label: There is no Chinese national admissions deadline for an international applicant, and the two intakes are not one cycle
deadlines.notes: China has no UCAS, no Common App and no ministry-run deadline for international undergraduates. The gaokao, which is the national examination the whole Chinese calendar bends around, is not a route a Danish IB candidate takes at all; international applicants are admitted by each university under its own 申请-审核 (application and review) procedure, on its own dates. Two things follow that the rest of this page depends on. First, every date below belongs to one institution and nothing generalises from it. Second, China runs two intakes — a September one, which is the main one and the one this profile covers, and a separate February or March spring intake which a smaller number of programmes offer. "2027 entry" on this page means September 2027 unless an entry says otherwise, and a deadline you find on a Chinese university's site may belong to the spring intake and be eight months out of step with the one you want. Check which intake a date is for before you plan around it. Note also that China's joint-venture universities — Duke Kunshan, NYU Shanghai, Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool, Nottingham Ningbo, CUHK-Shenzhen, United International College, Wenzhou-Kean — run on an entirely different calendar from Tsinghua, Peking, Fudan and Shanghai Jiao Tong, and several run on the American one.

deadlines.label: Duke Kunshan University — Early Decision, and it is binding
deadlines.audience: international applicants — DKU states these must be non-Chinese citizens
deadlines.notes: Published with its full calendar year on DKU's English international-admissions site as "Early decision application deadline: November 2, 2026 (11:59pm ET)", which is 05:59 on 3 November in Denmark. Applications are made through the Common App, which DKU began accepting for the 2027 entry term in August 2026, and Early Decision on the Common App is binding: you may hold one Early Decision application only, and if admitted you withdraw the rest and enrol. DKU's own How to Apply page does not restate those terms, so the binding force comes from the Common App agreement you sign rather than from anything DKU publishes — read it before you file. There is no application fee. The CSS Profile is required if you are seeking financial aid, and DKU is test-optional for the 2026-2027 cycle. A warning that matters more than any of this: DKU runs two entirely separate admissions tracks on the same domain. The Chinese-language site (admissions.dukekunshan.edu.cn, 中文 – 中国学生) publishes a 综合评价 comprehensive-evaluation route with rounds closing 3 January and 5 February, for Chinese students. Those are not your dates. A Danish applicant uses the English site marked "English – International Students", and DKU states that international applicants must be non-Chinese citizens.

deadlines.label: NYU Shanghai — Early Decision I, and it is binding
deadlines.notes: NYU Shanghai publishes "November 1" and "11:59 p.m EST" with no calendar year, so the year here is read into the cycle this profile covers and the entry is marked provisional. It is binding, and NYU's wording is more specific than most: if you are admitted to the campus you named as your primary interest, "you must accept the offer within 25 days", and "If accepted, you'll also need to withdraw applications from other schools, and cannot submit new applications" — so an NYU Shanghai Early Decision admission in December ends your application season, including applications you have already paid for elsewhere. One Common Application covers all three of NYU's degree-granting campuses, New York, Abu Dhabi and Shanghai, which is why an Early Decision here binds you against the others. This entry replaces one that said "Exact dates not verified" against a site root.

deadlines.label: NYU Shanghai — Early Decision II, also binding
deadlines.notes: Published as "January 1" with no calendar year; the year is read into this cycle, hence provisional. Same binding terms as Early Decision I, in the same window as Regular Decision, and it exists for a student whose first binding choice turned them down in December. The 25-day acceptance rule and the requirement to withdraw every other application apply here too.

deadlines.label: Duke Kunshan University — Regular Decision
deadlines.audience: international applicants — DKU states these must be non-Chinese citizens
deadlines.notes: Published with its full calendar year as "Regular decision application deadline: January 4, 2027 (11:59pm ET)", which is 05:59 on 5 January in Denmark. Not binding: you keep every offer you hold and reply on 1 May 2027, which is its own entry below. The DKU application is the Common App plus two DKU-specific essays, and DKU also lets an applicant to Duke University in North Carolina share that application with DKU — but only the materials submitted at that moment are shared, and transcripts, school reports, recommendations and CSS Profile documents that arrive later must be sent to both universities separately. That is the detail most likely to cost somebody an assessed application.

deadlines.label: NYU Shanghai — Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Published on NYU Shanghai's How to Apply page as "Regular Decision - January 5", 11:59 p.m. EST, with no calendar year, so the year is read into this cycle and the entry is provisional. The Early Decision page leaves it out, which is why an earlier pass recorded it as not published. Read 23 September 2026.

deadlines.label: Duke Kunshan University — Regular Decision acceptance deadline
deadlines.audience: applicants holding a Duke Kunshan Regular Decision offer
deadlines.notes: Published on DKU's international-admissions homepage with its year as "May 1, 2027 (11:59 PM ET) — Regular Decision Acceptance Deadline". It is the same day as the American national candidates' reply date, which is no coincidence: DKU recruits against American colleges through the Common App and keeps their calendar. It falls more than two months before IB results are released, so the offer you accept is conditional on predicted grades, and what DKU does if your final results fall short is not published and has not been established here. Ask before you accept. An Early Decision admission does not get this date; that choice was made in November.

deadlines.label: Tsinghua University — international undergraduate admission, in three batches whose dates are behind a login
deadlines.audience: international applicants — Tsinghua requires a foreign passport, and foreign permanent residency does not qualify
deadlines.notes: Split out of a single entry that held Tsinghua, Peking, Fudan and Shanghai Jiao Tong together, because Tsinghua's shape is now established even though its dates are not. Tsinghua admits international undergraduates under 申请-审核, application and review, in three application batches. The batches take the same form and the same documents but have different application periods, different interview dates and different result dates, and applicants to the Design (设计学类) and Fine Arts (美术学类) programmes must apply in the first batch — so for those two, the earliest batch is the only batch. The dates themselves are not published on any open page: they live inside the online application system at apply.join-tsinghua.edu.cn, which requires an account before anything can be seen, and one email address may be registered only once per year. That is why this entry has no date. Two facts from Tsinghua's own Chinese-language applicant FAQ are more decision-relevant than any date and are recorded here because nothing else on this site says them: Tsinghua's undergraduate teaching is in Chinese (部分课程采用双语或英语教学 — some courses are bilingual or in English) with international students generally in the same classes as Chinese students, and the language requirement is HSK level 5 with at least 60 in every section, or HSK 4 on entry with HSK 5 to be reached within a year of enrolling or the place is withdrawn. Clinical Medicine does not take international undergraduates and Tsinghua accepts no transfer students. That FAQ is in Chinese only, has no English equivalent, and is dated to the 2017 cycle — so its structure is worth knowing and none of its numbers should be trusted for 2027. Confirm everything with admissions@tsinghua.edu.cn before building a plan on it.

deadlines.label: Peking University, Fudan University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University — international undergraduate admission
deadlines.notes: Not established, and the honest statement is that nobody has looked properly rather than that the dates do not exist. Three universities are held in one entry here because nothing in this record tells their dates apart, and that is a gap in the research and not a fact about China — each of the three runs its own application-and-review procedure on its own calendar, and they will not agree. What is known from the one comparable Chinese university whose structure has been read, Tsinghua, is the shape to expect: several application batches opening in the late autumn and closing between the winter and the early spring for a September intake, with art and design programmes restricted to the earliest batch, and the dates frequently published only inside a login-gated application system. What is needed to close this: each university's own international-student admissions page (留学生本科招生) read in Chinese, because the English pages are consistently thinner than the Chinese ones and in at least one case on this page are absent altogether. This Destination has no Evidence records at all — there is no data/evidence/cn.json — so every entry on this page stands on its source URL alone and none has been through the Evidence process the rest of the site uses.

deadlines.label: Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS/CSC) — and the official portal this site used to cite no longer exists
deadlines.notes: The Chinese Government Scholarship is applied for by one of three routes with three different calendars: Type A through the Chinese embassy in your country of residence, Type B directly to a CSC-designated Chinese university, and Type C through certain international organisations. Each embassy and each university sets its own closing date, so there is no single CGS deadline and this entry deliberately carries none. Two findings from 23 September 2026 matter more than a date. First, www.campuschina.org — the China Scholarship Council portal that this record previously cited as the source for both the scholarship and the domestic universities' deadlines, and which Chinese embassy notices still name as the application website — did not resolve: the domain returned NXDOMAIN to DNS lookup and ENOTFOUND to automated fetch, and the browser refused to navigate to it. It may have been retired, or it may be unreachable from northern Europe; either way nothing on this site should be sourced to it and nothing here now is. Second, the Chinese Embassy in Denmark's English site was read on the same day and publishes no Chinese Government Scholarship notice of any kind — no 2026/2027 notice and no 2027/2028 notice — so the Type A deadline that would apply to a student applying from Denmark is not established. What to do: from about October 2026, watch the Chinese Embassy in Denmark's own announcements for the 2027/2028 notice, and ask each university you are applying to for its Type B date at the moment you apply. Do not work from a deadline you find on another country's embassy page; they differ by months.

deadlines.label: IB results released
deadlines.notes: Recorded here because of where it sits rather than because anything in China is waiting for it. Every date on this page that has been established falls before it: Duke Kunshan closes Regular Decision in January and wants your acceptance on 1 May, and NYU Shanghai's binding early rounds are decided in December. So a Chinese joint-venture offer, like an American one, is made on predicted grades and accepted before you have real ones, and what happens if the results fall short is set by each university and is not established here. The Chinese universities' own timing is unknown for the same reason their deadlines are. The date is inferred rather than cited, and both the inference and the reason it could not be checked are held once, in data/ib-calendar.json with the Evidence record ev-ib-results-day-2027-05. It is marked provisional here for that reason.

steps: Decide first whether you want a Mandarin-medium education with a preparatory language year, or an English-medium joint-venture degree. They are different projects with different calendars.
For the joint-venture universities, work to the American calendar: shortlist in September 2026, apply by early November for Early Decision or early January for Regular Decision.
For a domestic university, check the HSK Chinese requirement for your intended programme before anything else, and budget for a preparatory year if you do not have it.
If you want a Chinese Government Scholarship, decide early between the embassy route and the university route — you normally cannot use both, and the embassy route closes earlier.
Prepare the standard international pack: IB transcript and predicted grades, personal statement, references, passport copy, a physical examination record, and a non-criminal record certificate.
Once admitted, the university issues a JW201 or JW202 form and an admission notice; you apply for an X1 student visa at the Chinese embassy in Copenhagen.
Within 30 days of arrival, convert the X1 visa into a residence permit at the local Public Security Bureau and complete the medical examination.
application.selectionNotes: NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan are selective on the American model — essays, references, interviews, holistic review — and both admit small cohorts split between Chinese and international students. XJTLU, Nottingham Ningbo and CUHK-Shenzhen apply their parent university's published requirements and are more predictable. Tsinghua and Peking are highly selective even in the international pool.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Concentrated in the joint-venture universities. XJTLU alone lists over 60 English-taught undergraduate programmes; NYU Shanghai, Duke Kunshan, Nottingham Ningbo, CUHK-Shenzhen and Wenzhou-Kean teach entirely in English. The domestic elite universities offer only a handful, mostly in economics, international relations and Chinese studies.
language.englishProof: The joint-venture universities apply their parent institution's requirements, where IB English is normally accepted. Domestic universities vary. Not verified.
notes: At the joint-venture universities you do not need Mandarin to enrol, but all of them require you to study it, and NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan build Chinese language into the degree.

At the domestic universities, HSK 4 to 6 is the normal requirement for a Chinese-taught degree. Many international students spend a funded preparatory year reaching it — the Chinese Government Scholarship includes this.
Four years of immersion is the fastest realistic route to genuine working Mandarin, and that is the single strongest non-academic argument for studying in China.

tuitionEuEea.value: China does not differentiate by EU status. International students pay an international rate at domestic universities; joint-venture universities charge a single fee to everyone. See tuitionNonEu.

notes: No Chinese tuition figure could be verified from an official page in this research. Every figure is left blank here rather than guessed at.

The structure to expect: domestic universities charge an international-student tuition rate per year that is low by Western standards, plus accommodation in a designated international dormitory. Joint-venture universities charge considerably more — NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan approach American levels, XJTLU and Nottingham Ningbo sit in between.
Living costs in Beijing and Shanghai are moderate by European standards; Suzhou, Ningbo, Kunshan and Zhuhai are considerably cheaper.
Most universities require international students to buy a specified Chinese medical insurance policy as a condition of registration — budget for it separately.

funding: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC), administered by the China Scholarship Council — the main government scheme, covering bachelor's degrees. Two routes: Type A through the Chinese embassy in Copenhagen, and Type B directly through a participating university. It normally covers tuition, on-campus accommodation, a monthly living stipend and comprehensive medical insurance, and can include a preparatory Chinese language year. None of these amounts could be verified in this research — confirm with the embassy.
Confucius Institute Scholarships fund Chinese language and teaching-related degrees specifically.
Provincial and municipal government scholarships (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) are separate schemes with their own applications, often administered by the university.
Duke Kunshan offers merit scholarships, need-based financial aid and a named Duke Kunshan University Full Scholarship. Terms not verified.
NYU Shanghai offers scholarships and financial aid to international students; details not verified.
XJTLU and Nottingham Ningbo run entrance scholarships based on academic performance at admission.
Danish SU: a full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules. Check su.dk before budgeting.
workRights: Students on a residence permit for study may take part-time work or internships only with the explicit endorsement of both the university and the exit-entry administration, recorded on the residence permit. The rules are restrictive and were not verified from an official source in this research. Do not plan to fund yourself by working.
residency: EU citizenship gives no shortcut. Once admitted you receive an admission notice and a JW201 (scholarship students) or JW202 (self-funded) form, which you take to the Chinese embassy in Copenhagen for an X1 visa. Within 30 days of arrival you must convert it into a residence permit at the local Public Security Bureau, which requires a medical examination at a designated Chinese facility — a foreign medical certificate is usually not accepted. The permit is renewed annually.
housing: Domestic universities house international students in designated international student dormitories on or near campus, which is the standard arrangement and is cheap. The joint-venture universities house undergraduates in modern residence halls — Duke Kunshan and NYU Shanghai both operate residential campuses. Renting privately as a foreign student is possible but involves police registration of your address within 24 hours of moving.
healthcare: International students are normally required to buy a specified Chinese medical insurance policy as a condition of registration, and to pass a medical examination as part of the residence permit process. Public hospitals are inexpensive but crowded; international clinics in Beijing and Shanghai are good and expensive. Your Danish EHIC does not apply.

institutions.name: Tsinghua University
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number, including the Bachelor of Economics and Management track and the Schwarzman-adjacent international programmes. Most undergraduate teaching is in Mandarin. Verify programme by programme.
institutions.note: China's most prestigious university and one of the strongest engineering schools in the world. International undergraduate admission is a separate process, but English-taught bachelor's provision is thin — most international undergraduates study in Chinese after a preparatory year.

institutions.name: Peking University
institutions.englishBachelors: Very limited. Yuanpei College is PKU's liberal-arts honours college but teaches principally in Chinese. The Yenching Academy is a one-year master's programme, not an undergraduate route. Most international undergraduates study in Mandarin.
institutions.note: China's oldest modern university and its intellectual centre, on a classical lakeside campus. Be clear about what is on offer: Yenching is postgraduate and Yuanpei is Chinese-medium, so PKU is realistically a Mandarin-language destination.

institutions.name: Fudan University
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number of English-taught bachelor's programmes, historically including clinical medicine (MBBS) and some economics and international relations tracks. Verify directly.
institutions.note: Shanghai's leading comprehensive university, traditionally the strongest in China for the humanities and social sciences alongside PKU. Its English-taught MBBS is one of the better-known English-medium medical degrees in Asia.

institutions.name: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited. Some English-taught tracks exist in engineering and medicine; the SJTU-ParisTech Elite Institute of Technology teaches in French and Chinese. Verify directly.
institutions.note: China's strongest engineering university after Tsinghua, and the institution that created the Academic Ranking of World Universities. Its joint institutes with Michigan and with ParisTech are the most internationally accessible parts.

institutions.name: NYU Shanghai
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught entirely in English, across business, data science, computer science, humanities, social science, neuroscience and interactive media arts. Awards an NYU degree and a Chinese degree.
institutions.note: A full NYU campus in Pudong with a student body split roughly half Chinese and half international, from more than 70 countries, and semesters available across NYU's global network. Every student studies Mandarin. Deadlines follow the American calendar via the Common Application.

institutions.name: Duke Kunshan University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught in English, across a liberal arts and sciences curriculum with interdisciplinary majors. Graduates receive both a US degree and a Chinese degree.
institutions.note: The clearest English-taught route into China for a 2027 start: Early Decision 2 November 2026, Regular Decision 4 January 2027, acceptance by 1 May 2027. Test-optional, with merit scholarships, need-based aid and a full scholarship available. Between Shanghai and Suzhou on the high-speed line.

institutions.name: Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University
institutions.englishBachelors: Over 60 undergraduate programmes, all taught in English, across engineering, science, business, humanities, film and design. Graduates receive dual XJTLU and University of Liverpool degrees.
institutions.note: By far the widest English-taught undergraduate choice in mainland China, with a dual Chinese and British degree and 2+2 or 2+1+1 routes that let you finish in Liverpool. Suzhou is an hour from Shanghai and much cheaper. The most practical option here for most IB students.

institutions.name: University of Nottingham Ningbo China
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught in English, awarding a University of Nottingham degree. Business, engineering, international studies, education and science.
institutions.note: The first foreign university to open a full campus in China, in 2004, awarding the same Nottingham degree as the UK with the option to transfer to the Nottingham or Malaysia campus. Ningbo is a comfortable port city south of Shanghai.

institutions.name: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught in English, across science and engineering, management and economics, humanities and social science, data science, medicine and music. Awards a CUHK degree.
institutions.note: A full mainland campus of the Hong Kong university, awarding the CUHK degree, in Shenzhen — China's technology capital and thirty minutes from Hong Kong. Residential college system on the Hong Kong model.

institutions.name: Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught entirely in English, in a whole-person liberal arts model: business, culture and creativity, humanities and social science, science and technology.
institutions.note: The first full-scale joint-venture liberal arts college in mainland China, founded by Beijing Normal and Hong Kong Baptist universities. Small, English-medium, residential, and in Zhuhai next to Macau — substantially cheaper than the Shanghai options.

institutions.name: Wenzhou-Kean University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught in English by an American faculty, awarding both a Kean University (New Jersey) degree and a Chinese degree. Business, computer science, architecture, psychology, biology and education.
institutions.note: An American public university's full Chinese campus, awarding the US degree, with small classes and an American curriculum. Considerably cheaper and less selective than NYU Shanghai or Duke Kunshan, and a genuine route to a US qualification.

institutions.name: Zhejiang University
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited at the main university; the ZJU-UoE Institute (with Edinburgh) and ZJU-UIUC Institute (with Illinois) at the Haining International Campus teach in English and award dual degrees.
institutions.note: One of China's top five universities, in Hangzhou — Alibaba's home city. Its International Campus at Haining, with Edinburgh and Illinois, is the English-taught entry point and awards dual degrees.

institutions.name: Tongji University
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number of English-taught bachelor's programmes, historically in civil engineering and architecture. Verify directly.
institutions.note: Founded as a German-Chinese medical school and still the most German-connected university in China, with Sino-German institutes and exchange routes. The strongest Chinese university for architecture and civil engineering.

institutions.name: Sun Yat-sen University
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited. Some English-taught medicine and business tracks; most undergraduate teaching is in Mandarin. Verify directly.
institutions.note: Southern China's leading comprehensive university, across three cities in the Pearl River Delta, with particular strength in medicine and marine science. Chinese-medium for most purposes.
